newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends up on fund buying, soyoil down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends up on fund buying, soyoil down.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended higher Tuesday on commodity fund buying and soyoil ended with modest losses on commercial selling, traders said.
"There was some serious fund buying in the meal," said one trader.
Floor sources estimated that commodity funds bought as many as 1,800 lots of soymeal on the day.
The long-term demand outlook for U.S. soymeal is healthy because world demand for protein remains high but South American suppliers are running out of soymeal, floor traders said.
On Tuesday, traders in Asia said China bought 30,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for December/January shipment.
"We're going to see prices hold up for a while," said a trader. "The demand is there."
In other export business, Egypt bought 21,000 of sunflowerseed oil for shipment during the second half of September, sources there said.
December soyoil ended down 0.04 cent per lb at 22.74 cents and others were down 0.01 to 0.05 cent. December soymeal was up $5.90 per ton at $204.60 and other contracts were $4.00 to $7.10 higher.
Soyoil futures were also underpinned by cool weather in the U.S. Midwest this week because it could mean lower soyoil yields, traders and analysts said.
In other export business, the Commodity Credit Corporation said it will tender on August 26 to buy 3,000 tonnes of U.S. soymeal for donation to the Republic of Georgia.
On the day in soyoil trade, ADM sold 100 lots September and 100 December, Cargill sold 200 lots of December and Central Soya sold 100 September, traders said.
In soymeal trade on the day, Smith Barney sought 700 lots December and 200 August and Refco bought 500 lots December and 300 lots September, floor sources said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 22,000 lots, against Monday's 18,202. Soyoil volume was pegged at 13,000 lots, against Monday's 11,643.
